artists.biography: Cardiacs are an English band formed in 1977 and led by Tim Smith. Noted for their complex, varied and intense compositional style and for their eccentric, theatrical stage shows, they have been hailed as an influence by many newer groups and artists.  Their music combines the excitement and energy of punk with the intricacies and technical cleverness of early British progressive rock, a combination sometimes referred to as pronk, although frontman Tim Smith has disavowed this classification.  Cardiacs have released eight studio albums plus a number of live albums, compilation albums and singles between 1980 and 2007, and are best known for the 1988 minor hit single "Is This the Life?" They are also noted for attracting strongly diverse responses: they have remained one of Britain's leading cult rock bands during their four-decade-spanning career, but have also attracted virulent critical attack (including a lengthy editorial ban from the British music magazine New Musical Express).  The band has been on indefinite (and possibly permanent) hiatus following the 2008 hospitalisation of Tim Smith after a heart attack and series of strokes.

perplexity.description:
The Seaside is a 1984 demo album by English rock band Cardiacs, representing the band's third demo release and an early milestone in their experimental rock catalog. Recorded between 1980 and 1983, the album showcases the band's distinctive approach to rock music during a formative period before their later studio albums established them as cult figures in progressive and avant-garde rock circles. Released through Alphabet Business Concern, the album features thirteen tracks that demonstrate the band's idiosyncratic compositional style and instrumental approach.

The album remained relatively obscure for decades until 2015, when it received a comprehensive reissue titled The Seaside: Original Edition. This expanded reissue included a new remaster from the original tapes, offering improved sound quality with enhanced bass and kick drum presence compared to the treble-heavy 1995 CD release. The reissue came during an extended period of band inactivity following Tim Smith's cardiac arrest in 2008, making it a significant release for longtime fans. The 2015 edition was released both digitally and as a deluxe box set featuring a photobook, replica cassette, lyric booklet, and archival materials from the original 1984 release period.

Critical reception of the reissue was positive, with reviewers praising both the improved audio quality and comprehensive packaging. Critics noted that the remaster successfully captured the sound closer to the original cassette release, with one reviewer describing the experience of hearing the remastered tracks as akin to discovering Cardiacs anew.
